templates.text: House A is worth £[[A]] and House B is worth £[[B]]. This year A rises by [[p]]% and B rises by [[q]]%. Which house gains more in £, and by how much? (4 marks)
templates.answer: A gains £[[A * p / 100|dp:2]], B gains £[[B * q / 100|dp:2]]; [[A * p > B * q|if:A/B]] gains more by £[[abs(A * p - B * q) / 100|dp:2]]

templates.text: A laptop costs £[[A]]. In a sale the price is reduced by [[p]]%. Mia has £[[m]]. Does she have enough money to buy it? Show your working. (3 marks)

templates.text: A shop increases the price of a £[[A]] jacket by 10% and then decreases the new price by 10%. Is the final price £[[A]]? Explain.
templates.answer: No: £[[A]] × 1.1 × 0.9 = £[[A * 0.99|dp:2]], which is 1% less than the original

templates.subtopic: Find the original value given a percentage
templates.source: Y8 Spring B3 Percentages · S11 Find the original value given a percentage
templates.text: A television costs £[[A * (1 - p / 100)|dp:2]] in a sale after a [[p]]% reduction. Ali works out [[p]]% of £[[A * (1 - p / 100)|dp:2]] and adds it on. Explain his mistake and find the original price.
templates.answer: The [[p]]% is of the original price, not of the sale price. Original = £[[A * (1 - p / 100)|dp:2]] ÷ [[1 - p / 100]] = £[[A]]
